title: Over 8,000 affected by water supply disruption
originalTitle: Over 8,000 affected by water supply disruption
content:
More than 8,000 South East Water customers have been affected by water supply issues across various parts of Kent.

Residents have been told it could be a couple of days before their water supplies are restored after four days of disruption.

The worst affected areas are Cranbrook and Benenden.

Bottled-water stations will re-open later in Cranbrook, Canterbury, Challock and Herne Bay - though South East Water says most customers in Herne Bay should have their supplies back.

The firm said its staff were exhausted and "pushed to limits" as they attempted to restore water across the county.

South East Water said issues were a result of prolonged hot weather, high demand, recent pipe bursts, and overnight power issues.

Mike Pickard, incident support manager at the water company, told BBC South East on Monday: "It's an ongoing challenge for us at the moment and we apologise sincerely to all affected customers."

He admitted the situation was "unacceptable" but said the firm was doing everything it could.

He added: "Our team is exhausted and being pushed to limits to make sure water is running."
